name: Concert Grand Piano
shortDescription: 88-key acoustic keyboard instrument featuring escapement hammers, high-tension cast iron plate, and tapered soundboard.
description: The grand piano is one of the most mechanically complex acoustic machines in history. Striking a key propels a felted wooden hammer through an escapement mechanism into high-tension steel strings, transferring over 20 tons of frame tension into a crowned solid spruce soundboard.
historicalOrigins: Invented by Bartolomeo Cristofori in Padua, Italy around 1700 as the 'gravicembalo col piano e forte' (harpsichord with soft and loud).
acousticPrinciples: Impulse excitation: Felt hammer compression creates nonlinear attack profile
Dual-phase decay: Vertical and horizontal string polarization modes cause rapid initial decay followed by singing sustain
Inharmonicity: String stiffness slightly spreads upper partial frequencies (fn = n·f0·√(1 + B·n²))

characteristics.timbralColor: Expansive, crystalline, bell-like attack with warm resonant foundation
characteristics.orchestralRole: Solo concerto centerpiece, polyphonic harmonic foundation, chamber anchor

soundDNA.exciter: Felt-covered hardwood hammer launched via double-escapement repetition action
soundDNA.resonator: Solid sitka spruce crowned soundboard glued to multi-laminate hardwood rim
soundDNA.harmonics: Rich harmonic series with slight positive inharmonicity due to steel wire flexural stiffness
soundDNA.attackDecay: Instant percussive strike (~2ms) with prolonged dual-slope decay up to 20 seconds
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Massive dynamic range with thunderous bass and ringing crystalline treble
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Upward acoustic projection reflecting off open angled lid toward concert audience

piano_case.label: Grand Rim & Case
piano_case.function: Structural perimeter rim curved under steam pressure; reflects acoustic energy back into soundboard.

characteristics.material: Multi-ply Hard Rock Maple and Beech with polyester lacquer

lid.label: Acoustic Reflection Lid
lid.function: Directs sound waves radiating from soundboard outward toward the audience.

characteristics.material: Solid spruce core with hardwood veneer and brass prop stick

soundboard.label: Crowned Soundboard & Ribs
soundboard.function: Translates string vibrations into sound pressure; crowned with upward arch to resist downward string bearing.

characteristics.material: Quarter-sawn close-grained European or Sitka spruce

iron_plate.label: Cast Iron Harpsichord/Harp Plate
iron_plate.function: Withstands 18–22 metric tons of string tension without distorting the wooden cabinet.

characteristics.material: Grey iron sand casting finished in antique gold lacquer

strings.label: High-Tension Piano Strings
strings.function: Oscillating steel wire (plain treble wires in unisons of 3; copper-wound bass strings).

characteristics.material: High-tensile Röslau steel wire wound with pure copper

hammers.label: Escapement Action & Hammers
hammers.function: Propels wool-felt hammerheads toward strings and instantly escapes to avoid damping vibration.

characteristics.material: Hornbeam shanks with dense compressed virgin wool felt

keys_white.label: Diatonic Natural Keys
keys_white.function: Front-line user control levers transferring finger force into the repetition whippen.

characteristics.material: Quarter-sawn Bavarian spruce topped with synthetic ivory (Ivorite)
characteristics.mechanism: Balanced first-class lever with lead counterweights

keys_black.label: Accidental Sharp/Flat Keys
keys_black.function: Elevated chromatic keys providing full 12-tone equal temperament access.

characteristics.material: Dense African Gabon Ebony or matte composite

pedals.label: Lyre Pedals (Sustain, Sostenuto, Una Corda)
pedals.function: Lifts dampers off strings (sustain), catches selected notes, or shifts keyframe sideways (soft pedal).

characteristics.material: Solid cast brass pedals with hardwood trapwork levers
characteristics.role: Sympathetic resonance and acoustic timbre modulation

followTheSound.title: Key Depression
followTheSound.explanation: Pianist strikes a key, tilting the lever and lifting the damper off the vibrating string.

followTheSound.title: Hammer Strike & Escapement
followTheSound.explanation: The jack launches the hammer toward the string; escapement trips just 2mm before contact, allowing natural rebound.

followTheSound.title: Unison String Oscillation
followTheSound.explanation: Hammer impact initiates transverse waves across three unison strings, exchanging energy through the bridge.

followTheSound.title: Soundboard Driving
followTheSound.explanation: Vibrations transfer through hardwood bridges into the crowned spruce soundboard, projecting deep dynamic volume.

followTheSound.title: Acoustic Radiation & Projection
followTheSound.explanation: Soundboard waves radiate upward, bounce off the propped wooden lid, and fill the auditorium with immersive stereo depth.
